caption: A square of chocolate lies in a skillet over low heat, and it melts into a spreading pool.

sa.check: A square of chocolate lies in the skillet.
The square melts: it goes glossy and loses its edges.
A pool of chocolate spreads around it.
The square starts with straight sharp edges.
The melting comes first and the pool follows.

pc.expect: The square only softens and shrinks while the pool grows; nothing hardens again in the warm pan.
pc.fail: The square regains its sharp edges; or the pool draws back into the square; or the chocolate sets firm and matt again in the pan; or the square alternates between firmer and softer.

pc.expect: The melted chocolate is a thick glossy liquid that flows slowly and levels, and the square is a soft solid that slumps and smears.
pc.fail: The melted chocolate runs as thin as water; or the square shatters into dry shards; or the pool stands as a rigid dome; or the square keeps sharp edges while glossy and flowing.

pc.expect: The pool spreads outward and downhill across the pan's floor and runs to its low side.
pc.fail: The pool climbs the pan's wall and stays; or a run travels uphill; or melted chocolate lifts off the pan and floats.

pc.expect: The square melts where it touches the pan: it goes glossy underneath first and the pool spreads from beneath it.
pc.fail: The square melts from its top face while its underside stays matt and sharp; or a pool spreads on a part of the pan the square never touched; or the square slumps while the pan around it stays dry.

pc.expect: One square; the chocolate goes only into the pool.
pc.fail: The square grows; or a second square appears; or the square vanishes while still whole; or chocolate appears across the pan with none flowing there.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pool keeps the square's dark colour, and the pan's finish and the hob stay the same.
pc.fail: The chocolate turns pale; or the pan changes colour; or items around the hob rearrange.
